text.p: The compensation coupons rose to a new 52-week high of 770 forints on the Budapest Stock Exchange on Thursday, traders said.
They added that they saw planned share for compensation coupon swaps as the driving force behind the coupon's strengthening.
"Investors are buying coupons on preparations for swaps in Forte and Szabolcstej," one trader said.
Coupons opened at 700 forints, below Wednesday's close of 710 forints and reached 770 before easing slightly to 767 forints at 1145 gmt.

Hungary's privatisation agency APV Rt announced a one-round public tender earlier this month for the management of the public offer in stakes in Forte Fotokemiai Rt photographic industrial and Szabolcs Tejipari Rt dairy industrial companies.

APV said it planned to offer a 49.32 percent stake, worth a nominal 531.2 million forints, in Forte and a 45.08 percent stake, worth a nominal 229.2 million forints, in Szabolcstej for a mixture of cash and coupons.
Compensation coupons were awarded to victims of expropriations and persecutions under Hungary's former fascist and communist regimes.
